identity.title: Jailbreak Foundry: From Papers to Runnable Attacks for Reproducible Benchmarking

problem.claim: LLM jailbreak techniques evolve faster than benchmarks, making robustness estimates stale and cross-paper comparisons difficult amid drift in datasets, harnesses, and judging protocols.

gap.claim: Existing benchmarking lacks a unified way to translate new jailbreak papers into executable modules and evaluate them consistently.

contributions.claim: Introduces JAILBREAK FOUNDRY, a multi-agent workflow for translating jailbreak papers into executable modules within a unified evaluation harness.
Provides JBF-LIB for shared contracts and utilities, JBF-FORGE for paper-to-module translation, and JBF-EVAL for standardized evaluation.
Automates attack integration and standardized evaluation to support scalable, living benchmarks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish JBF as an automated, multi-agent system that converts jailbreak papers into runnable modules for immediate evaluation in a unified harness.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report reproducing 30 attacks with a mean reproduced-minus-reported ASR deviation of +0.26 percentage points.
The authors report reducing attack-specific implementation code by more than half relative to original repositories, with an 82.5% mean reused-code ratio.
The authors report standardized AdvBench evaluation of all 30 attacks across 10 victim models using a consistent GPT-4o judge.

narrative_sequence.summary: Jailbreak methods outpace benchmarks, causing stale and difficult-to-compare robustness estimates.
JBF addresses this gap by translating papers into executable modules through a multi-agent workflow and unified harness.
The system is organized into shared infrastructure, translation, and evaluation components.
Across 30 attacks, the authors report close mean ASR alignment, substantial code reuse, and standardized evaluation across 10 models.
The authors position automated integration and evaluation as a route toward scalable living benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a reproducibility-oriented system description with concrete alignment, code-reuse, and standardized-evaluation metrics.

lessons.interpretation: A paper-to-system claim becomes more assessable when operational outputs and multiple dimensions of evidence are stated together.
lessons.application: For a benchmarking system, report fidelity to source results, implementation cost or reuse, and coverage under a fixed evaluation protocol.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the work is purely theoretical or when source results and evaluation protocols cannot be meaningfully aligned.

unknowns: The abstract gives a mean ASR deviation but not its distribution, per-attack failures, or conditions explaining discrepancies.
Details of the 10 victim models, attack implementations, AdvBench setup, and GPT-4o judging procedure are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish independent verification, reproducibility by third parties, or priority over related systems.
